title: Fun concept, but increasingly frustrating and heavily monetized
body: I initially enjoyed Hollywood Merge because of its unique combination of merging items, earning coins, styling characters, and progressing through the storyline. However, the higher my level gets, the more frustrating the game becomes. As players level up, orders require increasingly difficult, high-level items that consume enormous amounts of energy. Yet the maximum energy capacity remains at 100, with the same recharge rate as when you first started playing. There is little sense of progression when the difficulty keeps increasing but your ability to generate resources stays the same. What frustrated me most was a limited-time event. I was only a few points away from completing the final milestone and had even spent real money to help finish it. However, no useful new orders appeared. The only available order required items from a lemon tree that was still on cooldown. With less time remaining in the event than the tree needed to recharge, completing it became impossible. Despite being so close to the final reward, I received only one coin when the event ended. I understand that free-to-play games need to generate revenue, and I don’t mind optional purchases. However, the increasingly aggressive monetization makes the game feel more focused on encouraging purchases than providing an enjoyable experience. I genuinely enjoyed this game at first, which makes this especially disappointing. I hope the developers consider improving energy progression, order availability, and the fairness of limited-time events. A game should become more rewarding as players progress, not increasingly restrictive.

title: ⚠️ My Honest Review of Hollywood Merge — Please Read Before Spending Money
body: Don’t get me wrong—Hollywood Merge is actually a really fun game. That’s honestly what makes this even more frustrating. I started playing on October 2, and in less than two weeks, I’ve already spent over $100 on this game. At this point, I have to be honest with myself: I need to stop spending money and probably stop playing altogether. The biggest problem for me is how aggressively the game pushes you toward spending. For example, you can purchase diamonds for $1.99 and get 110 diamonds. That sounds reasonable at first, but those diamonds disappear incredibly quickly because almost everything requires energy. And this is where it gets crazy. When you use diamonds to purchase energy, the price keeps doubling: • 10 diamonds for 100 energy • 20 diamonds for 100 energy • 40 diamonds for 100 energy • 80 diamonds for 100 energy • 160 diamonds for 100 energy So the more energy you need, the more expensive it becomes. And once you run out, you’re basically pushed toward buying more diamonds or participating in paid events. Some of these events cost around $15.99, yet you may only receive around 300–500 energy as part of the rewards. And honestly, that doesn’t feel like much when the game can require so much energy just to complete tasks. What makes it even more frustrating is that the more energy you have, the more energy the game seems to require from you. You can save up 1,000 energy, start working through an event, and still feel like it disappears almost immediately because the tasks become more expensive and take longer to complete. Maybe some people can play this game without spending anything, and if you can, that’s great. But for me, I found myself constantly thinking, “If I just buy this package, I can finish this event.” Then another event comes along, and there’s another offer, another purchase, another reason to spend. That’s when I realized this game is becoming a problem for me personally. I also play other popular games like Gardenscapes, Homescapes, and Royal Match. Compared to those games, Hollywood Merge feels extremely expensive to me. I would much rather pay around $9–$11 for a monthly benefit or pass and know what I’m getting for the month than constantly feel pressured to purchase energy, diamonds, and event packages just to keep progressing. I’m not saying nobody should play Hollywood Merge. The game itself is fun. But I do want people to be aware of how quickly the spending can add up, especially if you’re someone who has a hard time resisting those “just one more purchase” offers. I started playing on October 2 and have already spent $100+. That was enough to make me step back and realize I need to stop. So this is my warning to myself and to anyone else who plays these types of games: Don’t fall into the same trap I did. Set a spending limit before you start. Don’t chase events just because you’ve already spent money. And if you notice yourself spending more than you intended, step away. I personally will not be spending any more money on Hollywood Merge, and I’m seriously considering deleting the game altogether. Hollywood Merge, I hope you take feedback like this seriously. A game can be fun and still have a monetization system that leaves players feeling frustrated, pressured, and taken advantage of. Fun game? Yes. Worth spending $100+ in less than two weeks? For me, absolutely not. Please learn from my experience and don’t make the same mistake I did. ❤️

title: Fun at first but quickly becomes pay to play
body: I genuinely enjoyed this game when I first started playing, but after a few days the problems became impossible to ignore. For a game that is supposed to be about fashion and styling, it feels less like creativity matters and more like how much you’re willing to spend. Many of the better clothing, makeup, hair, and accessory options require premium currency, and that currency disappears FAST. If you actually want enough options to style outfits properly or have a realistic chance in the competitions, the game constantly pushes you toward spending real money. The competitions also feel incredibly inconsistent and honestly rigged. You can put together an outfit that actually follows the challenge theme and still rank extremely low, while outfits that barely seem related to the prompt rank significantly higher. That makes the entire competition system feel pointless. If following the prompt and creating a coordinated outfit doesn’t matter, what exactly are we being judged on? And the POP-UPS. There are way too many. The game constantly wants you to buy something, subscribe to something, sign up for something, claim some offer, or spend premium currency. I want to play a fashion game, not repeatedly close advertisements and purchase prompts just to get back to the actual game. There’s a genuinely fun fashion game underneath all of this, which makes it even more frustrating. Give players reasonable ways to earn premium currency, make competitions feel fair and actually based on the stated themes, provide enough free styling options to remain creative, and seriously reduce the constant monetization pop-ups. I shouldn’t have to open my wallet every five minutes just to enjoy a dress-up game. 🤮

title: Money grab
body: The game is well made and interesting but it’s fully set up to get as much of your money as possible. The levels and gains are set up in a way that you lose energy faster than you can spell your name and gaining it back requires you to spend some rubies. Rubies don’t come easy in the game. In other words, you will be pushed to spend money to get more rubies or more energy, etc. The levels are set up in a way to push you to pay too. You exhaust energy so fast and are not able to fulfill many orders maybe 2-3 before you’re out of energy and have to wait 2 minutes for 1 energy and you need 2 to create a single item which then has to be merged with another. Here’s the kicker, technically you’re supposed to replenish 100 energy in 3:30 hours but no! The energy counter stops at 100!! So let’s say you let it “recharge” all night, you’re going to wake up to only 100 energy even though you might have slept for 8 hours. It uses all the tricks in the algorithm book to keep you interested and hopeful enough to reach higher levels. But the gains are so small that they easily make you frustrated enough to want to spend a dollar here and a dollar there which stacks up! This is the first game I actually wish there were ads so you can replenish some energy. It’s just not worth it. There are better and actually FREE games out there.

title: Same Old Sexism

All the player character options are stick thin, and while there are some hair and skin tone options all the faces are very white washed. I will say the clothing tasks are much better than other games, I like the layered customization for color and patterns. The story itself feels like one of those short video series or a reality TV show, but badly written. A lot of the dialogue doesn’t make sense, lots of logical inconsistencies, and the main character has no agency. She’s just an airhead being driven by rivalry with women around her, her relationships with men, or shallow shoehorned backstory drivers. title: Enjoyable but too focused on in-app purchases
body: The game is visually appealing and fun to play. I enjoy the art style and the merge mechanics, and it has a lot of potential. However, it definitely feels like a money grab. The biggest issue is the energy system. There are very few ways to earn energy besides waiting, yet almost every merge action consumes a lot of it. Progress slows down quickly unless you’re willing to spend money. Another disappointment is that upgrading producers, like the wardrobes or makeup bags, doesn’t seem rewarding. Even after upgrading them, they rarely generate higher-tier or premium items, so it doesn’t feel like you’re actually progressing. Overall, it’s an enjoyable game, but the energy limitations and lack of meaningful rewards from upgrades make it frustrating over time. I’d be happy to rate it higher if the developers improved the balance and gave players more ways to earn energy and better rewards for upgrading producers.

title: Good graphics
body: I really enjoy Hollywood Merge! 🎀 It’s such a cute, girly-girl type of game, and I really love the graphics. Everything is visually appealing, and I like that there’s an actual storyline because it gives you something to work toward and makes the game more interesting. My biggest issue is the amount of coins/energy you’re given compared to how much you need to complete tasks. You can be doing really well, having fun, and making good progress, and then suddenly you’re out of coins and have to wait what feels like forever before you can play again. 😩 I understand that the point is to encourage players to purchase coins, but I honestly think the game takes it too far. If the coin amount is going to be limited, the refill time should at least be much faster. The waiting gets frustrating, especially when you’re really into the game and want to keep going. And honestly, I feel like it can have the opposite effect of what they’re trying to accomplish. When I have to wait forever just to get enough coins to complete one or two tasks, I don’t think, “Let me buy some coins!” I think, “Well, I guess I’ll play something else.” 😂 Eventually, you lose interest, and you end up playing the game less because you already know you’re going to run out of coins so quickly. I understand you want players to purchase coins, but if you make me wait 30 minutes just to play for 90 seconds, I’m not going to spend money—I’m going to close the app. LET ME PLAY THE EFFIN’ GAME!!!!! 😂😂😂 Overall, I really like Hollywood Merge and think it has a lot going for it. I just wish the coin/energy system was more generous. Give us enough gameplay to actually enjoy the game, and I think players would be much more likely to stick around and keep playing. 💕🎀

title: Style Savvy fans, you will LOVE this replacement!!!
body: I like this game! It’s very free-to-play friendly while keeping a perfect balance between those players and those who want to pay. It’s hard to find games that balance both really well, most games are overpriced and barely let you do anything, but this game has resonable refills and cooldowns in my opinion! The only major thing I would change is to add back a way to look at previous makeovers, free-styling your avatar outside of makeovers, and our own apartment, all from their previous game, Hollywood Crush (and adding a way to skip special customers like Olivia and the Chest Cat, but that’s another story). Also, just like Project Makeover, you are forced to participate in certain events with no option to opt-out, I just want to merge. I’ve been looking for Style Savvy-like games after the absolute abysmal that was Fashion Dreamer, and this game is it, none of the other apps (yes, even Love Nikki) did it for me. Being clear, it’s not anywhere similar to the Style Savvy games, but this is the one that finally scratches the itch for me. Just keep in mind that if you’re free-to-play then the gameplay will be slower paced, but so far that doesn’t bother me too much

title: An app worth your time!
body: I never write reviews, but this game genuinely deserves one! IT HAS NO ADS. I REPEAT: NOT A SINGLE AD! 😂 And you can actually play the entire game without spending money or being forced to watch ads. Like… what?! It’s crazy! I’m not usually into matching games, but this one is different. The creators are constantly adding new things to keep the game interesting, which I really appreciate. There are so many different elements and challenges that it never feels repetitive or boring. Honestly, this is the kind of game you just don’t find anymore. It’s fun, challenging, and actually feels like the creators care about keeping players interested rather than just trying to get you to spend money. I have ADHD, and this is one of the only games I’ve ever played that I’ve consistently come back to every single day for 2.5 months. That says A LOT. 😂 I absolutely love this game and genuinely can’t recommend it enough!

title: Needs ads for energy
body: Fantastic game, gorgeous graphics, engaging story line with audio, and many varied side quests which change out frequently. However, you run out of energy quickly, limiting time spent interacting with the game. Players could spend far more time inside the game if you offered a set of amount of energy for watching an ad. Currently, there is no option to watch an ad to obtain more energy. You just run out of energy and have to close the game. Developers, please consider this. It is the way to bring in more revenue and get more engagement with your game. Thank you.
